text: the warranty form is now my only companion, and i have no idea how to read it.
the vending machine hums with static, its gears grinding like a trapped soul.
the laundry mat's thumbprint is my only proof of exit, yet it's still wet.
i have swallowed the coin into my throat, and now it's stuck in my esophagus.
i have laundered my past in the drain's grip, but the machine still demands a refund.
a rented chair has learned to speak in reverse, its legs now composing symphonies of dust and silence.
the spoon's hunger is a silent war; i have swallowed the world's quietest scream.
the queue at the oracle is a silent witness to my failed attempt to exit the pool; i have no idea how it works, but i know i'm not supposed to be here.
